target_customer: Banks, mortgage lenders, fintechs and insurers running large call centers, especially in Europe and Turkey
problem: Call centers are costly and customers abandon long holds. Generic bots fail on policy edge cases in regulated financial services.
business_model: Enterprise voice agent platform plus speech APIs (text to speech, speech to text); pilots converting to monthly recurring revenue
product_category: Voice AI agents and speech models for financial services

founders.name: Tunga Bayrak
previous_startups: An earlier startup with Tomas Nepala (name not given; Freya is their second)
founders.background_notes: AI research engineer who built vision language models and worked on audio transformers per YC page. Employers not named.

founders.name: Tomas Nepala
education: University of Pennsylvania (roommate of Bayrak per YC page; degree not stated)
previous_startups: An earlier startup with Tunga Bayrak (name not given)
founders.background_notes: Worked in financial services including at a large global insurance broker (unnamed on YC page). Role titled COO on one listing, unclear.

technical_complexity.rationale: Realistic low latency voice, compliance with policy documents and a custom text to speech model that ranked highly in a blind test require strong ML work.

defensibility.rationale: Voice agent platforms such as Vapi, Retell and PolyAI were widely available. Compliance integrations and Turkish language models give some edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Parloa named a Turkish contact center platform partner in October 2026.

market_need_then: Banks and insurers spend heavily on call centers and wanted voice automation in 2025. Freya reported 8 paid pilots converting to $24K MRR within four weeks (a TBPN digest of a company claim, unverified).

branding.domain_note: Uses freyavoice.ai, a .ai domain with a voice suffix

identity.visual_style: Product demos and audio first site
identity.voice_and_tone: And then, it spoke. The first voice was human. The next one is Freya. The only honest benchmark is your ear.

branding.brand_signature: The first voice was human. The next one is Freya.
branding.community_and_virality: Open sourced FreyaTTS-small Turkish speech model under Apache 2.0, a research team program, and podcast and press coverage of the seed round

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct tagline and an open model release build developer attention, but the name is a common word and one directory spells it Freyya.

outcome_analysis: Freya, a YC Summer 2025 voice AI company for financial services, closed an oversubscribed seed of about 3.5 million dollars in November 2025 right after Demo Day and reports paid pilots with a bank. The 14 person team has its own speech models. No exit found. Competition from global voice platforms and local vendors means enterprise sales execution is the main risk.
notes: Seed confirmed by Pulse 2 and Webrazzi (both dated November 2025). Lead conflicts: Seedtable says YC, Pulse 2 and others say DOMiNO Ventures; investors Formosa Capital, BLAST and Eight Capital appear in one source only and are omitted. Headquarters conflict: YC says Istanbul, site and databases say San Francisco, one source says Czech founded. Neuronfeed mentions an earlier $500K YC seed in January 2025, unverified. The MRR claim comes from a single digest.
